faq.sectionSubtitle: Frequently asked questions about O-ring standards, measurements, and conversions.

q1.question: What is the difference between AS568, JIS B 2401, and Metric O-ring standards?
q1.answer: AS568 is the North American standard based on fractional inches with standardized dash numbers. JIS B 2401 is the Japanese standard categorized into P (dynamic/packing), G (static/gasket), S (special dimensions), and V (vacuum) series. Metric O-rings are specified directly in millimeters (Inside Diameter × Cross Section) following international standards such as ISO 3601.

q2.question: How do I accurately measure an O-ring?
q2.answer: To identify an O-ring, measure two critical dimensions using a vernier caliper: Inside Diameter (ID) across the inner opening, and Cross Section (CS) across the cord thickness. Outside Diameter (OD) can be verified using the formula: OD = ID + (2 × CS).

q3.question: How do I calculate Outer Diameter (OD) from ID and CS?
q3.answer: The relationship is: Outer Diameter (OD) = Inside Diameter (ID) + 2 × Cross Section (CS). For example, an O-ring with 10 mm ID and 2 mm CS has an OD of 10 + 2(2) = 14 mm.

q4.question: How do I convert between millimeters and inches?
q4.answer: 1 inch equals exactly 25.4 millimeters. To convert inches to millimeters, multiply by 25.4. To convert millimeters to inches, divide by 25.4 (or multiply by 0.03937).
